주문 앱 새 버전이 배포된 오후, dbserver02의 CPU가 90%를: On the afternoon a new version of the order app was released, CPU on dbserver02 went over 90%. The number of orders being processed is about the same as yesterday. V$SQL shows thousands of statements that differ only in a number, such as order_id = 5100231 and = 5100232, each executed just once.
일의 양은 같은데 CPU만 늘었습니다. SQL을 \"실행\"하는 데가 아: The workload is the same, but CPU went up. That can mean the CPU is being spent not on executing SQL but on preparing to execute it. That preparation is parsing.
Database Performance Tuning Guide는 리터럴 값: The Database Performance Tuning Guide explains that SQL statements differing only in literal values cannot use the same shared SQL area, and that a hard parse needs additional CPU. This lesson turns those sentences into pictures.
+ 리터럴만 다른 SQL 수천 개: + thousands of SQL differing only in literals
SQL 하나가 실행되기까지: 파싱, 최적화, 로우 소스 생성, 실행: From SQL to result: parsing, optimization, row source generation, execution
SQL Tuning Guide는 SQL 처리를 네 단계로 나눕니다. <b: The SQL Tuning Guide divides SQL processing into four stages: parsing (checking the statement and looking for it in the shared pool), optimization (the optimizer chooses an execution plan), row source generation (turning the plan into an executable form), and execution.
이 일을 하는 것은 앱에 연결된 서버 프로세스입니다. 핵심은 둘째와 셋째: The server process connected to the app does this work. The key points are that the second and third stages are expensive, and that they can be skipped if the result of doing them once is already in the shared pool.
\"SGA·PGA와 백그라운드 프로세스\" 5장면에서 본 서버 프로세스가: The server process from scene 5 of "SGA, PGA and background processes" does this work. Both parsing and execution use the DB server's CPU, not the app's.
① 파싱 → ② 최적화 → ③ 로우 소스 생성 → ④ 실행: ① parse → ② optimize → ③ row source generation → ④ execute
파싱: 문법 확인, 의미 확인, 공유 풀 확인: Parsing: syntax check, semantic check, shared pool check
문서가 말하는 파싱은 세 가지 확인입니다. <b>문법 확인</b>은 SQ: Parsing, as the documentation describes it, is three checks. The syntax check confirms the SQL is grammatical (for example, FROM spelled correctly); the semantic check confirms the tables and columns exist and the user has privileges. The table and column information for the semantic check comes from the data dictionary cache in the shared pool.
마지막은 <b>공유 풀 확인</b>입니다. 문장 텍스트로 해시 값을 계산: The last is the shared pool check. A hash value is computed from the statement text to look for the same SQL already in the library cache. According to the documentation, this hash value is the SQL ID shown in V$SQL.SQL_ID.
문법이 틀리면 첫 확인에서, 없는 테이블이면 둘째 확인에서 오류가 납니다: A syntax error fails the first check; a missing table fails the second. A statement with an error never reaches execution.
공유 풀: 라이브러리 캐시와 데이터 사전 캐시: The shared pool: library cache and data dictionary cache
Database Performance Tuning Guide에 따르면 <: According to the Database Performance Tuning Guide, the library cache stores the executable form of recently referenced SQL and PL/SQL, and the data dictionary cache stores data dictionary information (tables, columns, users). Both are in the shared pool in the SGA.
공간은 한정되어 있어서, 오래 안 쓰인 항목은 밀려납니다(aged out: Space is limited, so entries not used for a while are aged out. If thousands of one-time statements come in, even frequently used SQL can be pushed out and need to be parsed again.
버퍼 캐시가 데이터 블록을 다시 읽지 않으려는 캐시라면, 라이브러리 캐시: If the buffer cache exists to avoid rereading data blocks, the library cache exists to avoid reparsing SQL.
+ 라이브러리 캐시: 실행 가능한 SQL·PL/SQL: + library cache: executable SQL and PL/SQL
찾으면 소프트 파스, 못 찾으면 하드 파스: Found: soft parse. Not found: hard parse
공유 풀 확인에서 같은 SQL을 찾으면 <span class=\"term: If the shared pool check finds the same SQL, it is a soft parse (a library cache hit). As the documentation says, a soft parse skips optimization and row source generation and goes straight to execution. If not, it is a hard parse (a cache miss): the optimizer builds a new plan and it is placed in the library cache.
하드 파스는 CPU를 더 쓸 뿐 아니라, 공유 풀의 구조를 고치는 동안: A hard parse not only uses more CPU, it must also hold serialization devices (latches and mutexes) so that changes to shared pool structures do not collide with other sessions. When hard parses pile up, time spent waiting for these devices grows too. library cache: mutex X in the Database Reference wait event list is a wait for such a mutex.
소프트 파스도 공짜는 아닙니다. 그래도 최적화를 건너뛰므로 하드 파스보다: A soft parse is not free either, but it skips optimization and is far cheaper than a hard parse. The goal is: SQL doing the same job is hard parsed only once.
공유 SQL 영역은 함께, 개인 SQL 영역은 세션마다: The shared SQL area is shared; each session has its own private SQL area
하드 파스의 결과(파스 트리와 실행 계획)는 라이브러리 캐시의 <span: The result of a hard parse (the parse tree and execution plan) goes into a shared SQL area in the library cache and is used by many sessions. Bind values and execution state, on the other hand, differ per session, so they are kept in the private SQL area in each server process's PGA. Concepts describes a cursor as a handle to this private SQL area.
같은 SQL 텍스트 하나(부모 커서) 아래에 계획이 여러 개(자식 커서): One SQL text (the parent cursor) can have several plans beneath it (child cursors). For example, the same text referring to a same-named table owned by a different user gets its own child cursor. CHILD_NUMBER in V$SQL is that number.
DBA 실습 9단계 레슨 71의 <code>dbms_xplan.displ: In DBA labs stage 9, lesson 71, dbms_xplan.display_cursor('8wzq2k1ptm6c4') reads the plan of exactly this shared SQL area in the library cache.
+ 개인 SQL 영역 (바인드 값, 상태) → PGA: + private SQL area (bind values, state) → PGA
\"같은 SQL\"은 글자 하나까지 같아야 한다: "The same SQL" must match to the last character
SQL Tuning Guide에 따르면 공유되려면 SQL 텍스트가 공백,: According to the SQL Tuning Guide, to be shared the SQL text must be identical character for character, including spaces, case and comments. SELECT versus select, or one extra space, makes a different statement. The documentation explains that a hard parse effectively recompiles the statement.
그래서 <code>order_id = 5100231</code>과 <co: So order_id = 5100231 and order_id = 5100232 are different SQL. As in the documentation example, three statements differing only in literals become three different parent cursors. The thousands of statements in scene 1 each went through a hard parse and each created its own cursor.
문서는 \"문법이 같다는 것만으로는 충분하지 않다\"고도 적습니다. 텍스: The documentation also says identical syntax alone is not sufficient: even with the same text, different objects or environments cannot use the same plan (the child cursors of the previous scene).
바인드 변수: 값은 바꾸고 텍스트는 그대로: Bind variables: change the value, keep the text
값 자리를 <code>:b1</code> 같은 <span class=\": Put a bind variable such as :b1 where the value goes, and the SQL text is always the same; only the value changes. It is hard parsed once on the first execution, then soft parsed to use the same shared SQL area. In the documentation example, the SQL with binds has a VERSION_COUNT of 1. The value lives in each session's private SQL area.
하드 파스할 때 옵티마이저는 바인드에 처음 들어온 값을 들여다보고(바인드: During the hard parse, the optimizer peeks at the first value supplied for the bind (bind peeking) to choose a plan. The documentation also describes adaptive cursor sharing for cases where the best plan depends on the value.
DBA 실습 레슨 71에서 앱이 보낸 SQL이 <code>TO_CHAR(: Recall that in DBA lab 71 the app's SQL was TO_CHAR(O.ORDER_DATE,'YYYYMM')=:B1. That means the app was using bind variables properly.
+ 하드 파스 1번, 그 뒤 소프트 파스: + one hard parse, then soft parses
사례: 새 버전이 값을 SQL 텍스트에 붙여 보냈다: Case: the new version glued values into the SQL text
1장면의 원인입니다. 새 버전 앱이 주문 번호를 바인드 변수로 넘기지 않: This is the cause from scene 1. The new app version did not pass the order number as a bind variable; it concatenated it into the SQL string. The SQL text differed for every order, so every execution was a hard parse, and that CPU and shared pool contention became the 90% CPU. You confirm it by a sharp rise in parse count (hard) and thousands of statements sharing the same beginning.
근본 해결은 개발팀이 바인드 변수로 고치는 것입니다. 그 전까지 문서에: The real fix is for the development team to switch to bind variables. Until then, the stopgap in the documentation is CURSOR_SHARING=FORCE, which replaces literals with system binds (:"SYS_B_0") so that similar statements share a cursor. The documentation notes that this setting does not reduce the parse count itself, so it does not replace fixing the app.
CURSOR_SHARING은 인스턴스 전체 SQL에 영향을 줍니다. 운영: CURSOR_SHARING affects all SQL in the instance. Changing it in production needs change approval, along with a plan to return to the original value (EXACT) once the app is fixed. Comparing parse statistics before and after the release in AWR reports makes it easier to explain to the development team.
정리: 한 번 파싱하고 여러 번 실행한다: Recap: parse once, execute many times
SQL은 파싱(문법·의미·공유 풀 확인), 최적화, 로우 소스 생성, 실: SQL goes through parsing (syntax, semantic and shared pool checks), optimization, row source generation and execution. If the same SQL is in the library cache of the shared pool, a soft parse skips optimization; if not, a hard parse has the optimizer build a new plan.
\"같은 SQL\"은 글자 하나까지 같아야 하므로, 값은 바인드 변수로: "The same SQL" must match to the character, so values are passed as bind variables to keep the text fixed. The plan is shared in the shared SQL area; bind values and execution state stay in each session's PGA.
